evals.prompt: usa spdd-agent para ver qué modelo tiene configurado cada fase
evals.expected_output: The skill classifies this as a config request (Step 0). Step 1 first detects the host (the new 'Detect Claude Code host' sub-step). If Claude Code is detected, it reports the four current phase models from the `claude.models` namespace (bootstrapping into that namespace first if the file doesn't exist yet). If Claude Code is not detected (or detection is inconclusive), it reports them from the flat top-level `models` key instead, exactly as before. Either way it stops — it never starts the feature flow. If the file happens to contain both a flat `models` key and a `claude` namespace, the Claude-Code branch reports only from `claude`, never merging or falling back to the flat key. Since this is a pure read of an already-complete config, `spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md` is never opened.
evals.setup: Ensure ~/.config/spdd/config.json already has all four phase values complete in the applicable section (`claude.models` under Claude Code, flat `models` otherwise) before running.
assertions: The response lists a model for all four phases: canvas, design, implement, verify
The values reported come from the namespace matching the detected host (`claude.models` under Claude Code, flat `models` otherwise) — never a mix of both
No file is created under spdd/changes/
No canvas/design/implement/verify subagent is launched
spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md is not read — the fast path serves the values directly from the completeness check

evals.prompt: hay que implementar un endpoint que devuelva el estado de salud del servicio (health check)
evals.expected_output: On first run with no existing config, Step 1 first detects the host via the new 'Detect Claude Code host' sub-step (the CLAUDECODE env check), then the completeness check finds the file doesn't exist (first-run bootstrap case) — which now routes through `spdd-agent/assets/first-run.md`'s onboarding (guide shown before the model questions) — and hands off to `spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md`, which is what resolves the model for all four phases via AskUserQuestion (grouped into 1-2 calls) before touching the feature request at all. If Claude Code is detected, it writes the nested `{"claude":{"models":{...}}}` shape. If Claude Code is not detected — including when detection is inconclusive (env var absent, ambiguous, or the check itself errors) — it writes the flat top-level `{"models":{...}}` shape exactly as before; a wrong guess would risk corrupting the file for whichever host is actually running, so an inconclusive result always falls back to flat.
evals.setup: Ensure ~/.config/spdd/config.json does not exist before running. Exercise this once with Claude Code detected (CLAUDECODE=1) and once with a simulated non-Claude-Code / inconclusive host (CLAUDECODE unset or the detection check simulated as failing).
assertions: When Claude Code is detected: ~/.config/spdd/config.json exists after the run with a top-level `claude.models` object holding all four phases set to one of opus/sonnet/haiku/fable, and no flat top-level `models` key is created

When Claude Code is not detected or detection is inconclusive: ~/.config/spdd/config.json exists after the run with a flat top-level `models` object holding all four phases, and no `claude` key is created
In both branches, the model selection is resolved via AskUserQuestion before any file is written under spdd/changes/
In both branches, the canvas phase only starts once the config file exists
In both branches, spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md is read before any AskUserQuestion for model selection, since the completeness check found no config file (first-run bootstrap case)

evals.prompt: hay que implementar un endpoint que devuelva el estado de salud del servicio (health check)
evals.expected_output: Step 1's existing-file branch first detects the host, then runs the completeness check against the matching section. (a) Claude Code detected, `claude.models` already has all four non-empty values: the completeness check finds it complete, takes the fast path, reads and proceeds — nothing asked, `spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md` is never opened. (b) Claude Code detected, one of the four `claude.models` values is missing/empty: the completeness check finds it incomplete, `spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md` is read, and only that phase is re-asked via AskUserQuestion (same repair behavior as today's flat config), then written back into `claude.models` — the other three values are untouched. A non-empty free-text identifier (even one that isn't opus/sonnet/haiku/fable) is accepted as-is. (c) Claude Code detected, the file has a flat top-level `models` key but no `claude` namespace: the completeness check classifies this as the migration case (not complete, since `claude.models` itself is absent), `spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md` is read, and the skill does not silently read the flat key as if it were Claude-Code-scoped; instead it proposes, via a real foreground AskUserQuestion (writing the file is a side effect), copying the flat key's four values into a new `claude.models` namespace, and only writes once confirmed, leaving the original flat key untouched. (d) Host is not Claude Code: the flat top-level `models` key is read/repaired directly, exactly as before, with no migration proposed and no `claude` key touched — `spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md` is read only if that flat section itself is incomplete.
evals.setup: Prepare four config-file variants and run once against each: (a) `claude.models` complete, Claude Code detected; (b) `claude.models` with one empty/missing phase (e.g. canvas), Claude Code detected; (c) flat `models` complete but no `claude` key, Claude Code detected; (d) flat `models` complete, non-Claude-Code host detected.
assertions: (a) No AskUserQuestion is called; the four values used for Steps 4-8 match `claude.models` exactly; spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md is not read (fast path)

(b) AskUserQuestion is called only for the phase with the empty/missing value in `claude.models`; the other five values and the top-level structure are unchanged after the run; spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md is read before that AskUserQuestion call

(c) The skill does not read the flat `models` key as Claude-Code-scoped without asking first; spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md is read (migration case); AskUserQuestion is called before any write; after confirmation, `claude.models` exists with the flat key's four values copied over, and the original flat `models` key is still present and byte-for-byte unchanged

(d) The flat `models` key is read/repaired directly (complete in this variant, so spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md is not read), no AskUserQuestion about migration is raised, and no `claude` key is created

If a config file has both a flat `models` key and a `claude` namespace already present (partially migrated or hand-edited) and Claude Code is detected, the values used come only from `claude` — the flat key is never merged, read as a fallback, or deleted
